utterances.text: While I was the director of the communal services in Prijedor, which, as I said, was a body of municipal administration, my daily contacts, during the working hours, obviously, were with the president of the Executive Board. At that time, it was the late Mr. Milan Kovacevic, a physician.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: May I ask for a break, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Mr. Witness, based on your testimony, especially page 46, from the beginning on and later on when you told us that you "didn't notice anything that would reveal to me the existence of that body, of that Crisis Staff," and other statements which from our perspective may be - may be - not true, the Trial Chamber decided proprio motu to warn you that you are still under the duty to tell the truth. And I have to tell you the consequences that may result from a failure to do so. I have to inform you, leaving out now the procedural prerequisites, that the maximum penalty for false testimony on a solemn declaration shall be a fine of 100.000 euros, or a term of imprisonment of seven years, or both. You should know and you should reflect about these possible consequences. Until now, nobody has started any investigations against you, but that what was your testimony until now may serve for the Prosecution as an initial suspicion for starting such investigations, this time based on the suspicion of false testimony. It is your right also to correct your testimony, if you so want. But please be aware of the maybe consequences. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can I now answer, please? May I be allowed to answer, please?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: If the question can be repeated, yes, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, I wasn't referring to the question put to me by the Defence; I wanted to respond to your warning, sir.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Yes, it's your right. Please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Before I started my testimony, I gave the solemn declaration, and I have told only the truth in my testimony. You and the other members of the Honourable Chamber have implied that you maybe thought I was not being truthful in my testimony. I don't know in which part you thought I was not telling the truth. Whatever I said, I can prove that it was the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: You will have the possibility - as we did it in the past, because we can't conclude your testimony today - to revisit the transcript of today, and then it is for you later on, if you so wish, to correct the one or other answer in context. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Mr. Dragic, correct me if I am wrong, but I believe that you said that you can corroborate all your allegations by documents.

utterances.speaker: MILOVAN DRAGIC
utterances.text: What I meant when I said that concerns the work, my work, in the institution, which was under the authority of the Executive Board. I meant the reports on the work of the department for communal services, which were sent to the president of the Executive Board, and these documents should have been filed by the recipient body. Secondly, the department for communal services has its own files. And all the documents that need to be filed under the law will show the activities of a physical body during a given period of time, what activities it had carried out, with whom it had contacts, or who it reported to.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction: A legal person.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You started, before the interruption of the Honourable Chamber, giving us the names of the people who were members of the Executive Board with whom you had contacts during the period between April and September 1992.

utterances.speaker: MILOVAN DRAGIC
utterances.text: Yes, I started giving you their names. I told you who the president of the Executive Board was. Other members of the Executive Board were as follows: They were all secretaries of respective municipal bodies. There was the secretary of economic affairs. His name was Ranko Travar, who had a degree in economics. The next one was the secretary for urban planning and urban affairs, housing affairs, and property affairs, Mr. Vojo Pavicic. He had a degree in law. The secretary of the secretariat for cadastre and geodesic affairs was Mr. Radenko Banovic, who had a degree in land surveying. These were the three most important secretariats. There was a another one, the secretariat for general administrative affairs. I am not sure, but I believe that the head of that secretariat was, at the time, Mrs. Vera Stojic, who had a degree in law.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Did all these people sit in the offices allocated to the heads of the respective secretariats?

utterances.speaker: MILOVAN DRAGIC
utterances.text: My contacts with the heads of the secretariats took place in the offices of the Executive Board of Prijedor Municipality. That is, in the offices occupied by the heads of the aforementioned secretariats. Those offices were occupied by the heads of the aforementioned administrative bodies before the war, during the war, and after the war. Even to this very day, these offices are still occupied by the heads of these departments. It is not, obviously, the same people, but the offices and the positions of their occupants are the same. The current heads of the administrative bodies, or as they are now called, according to the current law on local administration, heads of departments still sit in those rooms. Before the year 1992, they used to be known as the secretaries of secretariats, and now they are called "heads of departments," according to the new on local self-government and administration.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Was curfew -- a curfew introduced in Prijedor Municipality? Who Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. was it applied to, and how could one move about while curfew was in place?

utterances.speaker: MILOVAN DRAGIC
utterances.text: Yes, a curfew was introduced in Prijedor for all the citizens of Prijedor Municipality. And I believe that the curfew, as far as I can remember, was between 2200 hours and 0600 hours on the following morning. During the curfew, one was not allowed to move about. That is, civilians were not allowed to move about, regardless of their ethnicity. Civilians could only move about if they had a permit or an authorisation issued by the police.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [In English] It is a convenient time for today.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: The time is ripe for a break for today. Let me take the opportunity to kindly ask you not to contact anybody who may be a witness in this case or in other cases or other persons you know from former Yugoslavia, and especially not one representative of the one or the other parties when you are staying here until tomorrow morning at 9.00. In addition, I have to ask you to rethink your testimony on the existence of the Crisis Staff, all your knowledge about the setting up of a Crisis Staff, and the composition of a Crisis Staff, and your maybe working together with the Crisis Staff. This will be one of the decisive points whether or not to take measures as mentioned before, because these are the points where the Trial Chamber has reasons to believe that it can't be your full testimony, what you gave us today. And promising to tell the truth means also to add spontaneously all that what you know and not to hide knowledge. You should get in contact, please, with the representative of the Registry if you so wish to revisit today's transcript. In any event, you should have the possibility to do so, if need may be, with the assistance of an interpreter. But I believe you know very well what you testified on the existence of a Crisis Staff and what should be your reaction tomorrow. The trial stays adjourned until tomorrow, 9.00, in Courtroom Number I.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: at 1.47 p.m., to be reconvened on Thursday the 16th day of January, 2003, at 2.15 p.m.
